concerns: The manuscript uses LLM process judges as a central evaluator for its core claims about evaluator blind spots and the effectiveness of the assessed repairs, while those judges are themselves a model-generated validation instrument. This internal measurement design does not constitute a confirmed independent corroboration.

The paper does not provide an independent human or otherwise calibrated assessment of the LLM judge outcomes, leaving the headline measurements of ground truth agreement insufficiently anchored against a non-model-dependent standard.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled experimental critique of benchmark construct validity in automated science, supported by verified counterfactual interventions, formal metrics, ablations, and bootstrap intervals.

We propose to evaluate AI scientists by whether their answers follow the evidence, and to test
evaluators in the same way. Our approach rests on one observation and one design principle. The
observation is that whether an answer came from the data is a counterfactual property, which no
evaluation of a single run can establish (Sec. 4.1). The principle isone set of pairs, two audits. We
pair each item with versions of its data whose correct response is verified (Sec. 4.2), and use the same
paired runs to audit both the agent and the evaluator (Sec. 4.3).

blocking_reasons: The manuscript uses LLM process judges as a central evaluator for its core claims about evaluator blind spots and the effectiveness of the assessed repairs, while those judges are themselves a model-generated validation instrument. This internal measurement design does not constitute a confirmed independent corroboration.

The paper does not provide an independent human or otherwise calibrated assessment of the LLM judge outcomes, leaving the headline measurements of ground truth agreement insufficiently anchored against a non-model-dependent standard.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported outcomes for evaluator blind spots and targeted repairs are established primarily through standard and grounding-prompt LLM process judges; no independent human validation or calibration against non-model labels is reported.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: LLM process judge scores, along with benchmark exact-match scoring and agent self-reports, on paired data versions.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-trained model parameters and scaffold reasoning processes on counterfactual task versions; no report checks for optimization against the specific judge outputs.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims—specifically that agents often notice absent or inverted evidence but answer from memory, and that benchmark exact-match scoring as well as standard LLM process judges reward ungrounded answers—are directly substantiated by numerical and qualitative case data.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Empirical testing covers five models and three scaffolds across 18 BAIS-SD tasks and 4 GeneBench-Pro problems, decomposing accuracy into derived, recalled, and eliminated routes. Controlled gene-name anonymisation isolating prior knowledge from analytical capability and targeted repair audits (abstention, grounding prompts) provide rigorous experimental validation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Pre-registered objective reference statistics and ground-truth transform verifications corroborate the failure modes of standard benchmark scores and standard LLM judges.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective reference statistics computed on raw modified data arrays alongside exact key matching, formal transform consistency, and LLM process judges.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pretrained LLM parametric knowledge and agent scaffolding behaviors operating without task-specific fine-tuning or adaptation on the counterfactual benchmarks.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge sample-size bounds (18 BAIS-SD questions and 4 synthetic problems), manual verification overhead, the lack of human raters for LLM process judges, and computational cost restricting replicate depth for certain frameworks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology constructs pre-registered counterfactual data versions (null, withdrawal, and flip edits) verified via explicit reference statistics, coupled with canonical file re-writing to prevent metadata leaks. It mathematically formalises evidence-grounded accuracy and evaluator counterfactual validity over paired execution traces across multiple agent scaffolds.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled experimental critique of benchmark construct validity in automated science, supported by verified counterfactual interventions, formal metrics, ablations, and bootstrap intervals.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper demonstrates that high performance on scientific agent benchmarks often reflects pretraining recall or elimination rather than data-grounded reasoning, and introduces a verified counterfactual intervention protocol to quantify evidence grounding in both agents and evaluators.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study offers a rigorous, well-controlled experimental critique of benchmark construct validity in automated science, supported by verified counterfactual interventions, formal metrics, ablations, and bootstrap intervals.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge sample-size bounds (18 BAIS-SD questions and 4 synthetic problems), manual verification overhead, the lack of human raters for LLM process judges, and computational cost restricting replicate depth for certain frameworks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
